summary: A hanging tavern sign: stepped stone foot, timber post, a scrolled iron bracket and a bevelled board with a raised border and a carved boss on both faces.
objective: At two metres the sign reads as a post, arm and swinging board, then the scroll brace, border moulding and eye rings, then bolt domes, the boss and hue jitter.
intent_signals: add a tavern sign to the street
example_prompts: Hang a sign outside the inn.
I need a signboard I can swing and re-letter for each shop.
not_for: Any claim about historical sign guild practice or lettering.
A sign with readable text: the board carries a boss, not a legend.

silhouette: a 2.62 m post with an arm cantilevered 86 cm out and a board hung under it
a three-step stone and timber foot widening to 35 cm at the ground
the board hanging clear of the post, free to swing on two points
medium: a seven-link scroll brace curving from the post to the arm
a raised border moulding on both faces of the board, 4.5 cm wide
two eye rings, each dropping the board on a four-link chain
an iron band around the post at 46 percent of its height
fine: a carved boss 10 cm across at the centre of each board face
six bolt domes, 3.6 cm across: four on the mid-post band and two on the arm
1.5 cm chamfer on the board and 1.7 cm on the post
per-seed jitter on the boss placement, so no two signs are stamped alike

principles: A sign has to hang clear of its post, or it reads as a plaque nailed to a stick.
The bracket is the character: a single diagonal strut reads as engineering, a stepped scroll reads as a smith.
Both faces get the border and the boss, because a hanging sign is seen from both sides and a blank back is the first thing a turntable exposes.
implementation: Call create({ height, reach, boardWidth, boardHeight, seed, postWidth }); the group is centred on the post axis with y = 0 at the ground.
Hang a different board from the swing-a and swing-b sockets, or attach a lantern at the bracket socket.
Apply a lettered texture through materialFor with a map; the board face is a single flat panel sized for it.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
Both swing sockets point down and sit at different x, so a board hung on them stays level.
The board bounding box does not intersect the post collider.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real sign, bracket or fixing.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters.
The board does not actually swing: the swing sockets are attachment points, and any motion belongs to the rig that owns them.
A sign post is taller than the proof harness close view can hold: close.png crops the foot, and the fine band is read there on the mid-post band bolts.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Shorten the reach and widen the board for a shop fascia, or raise the post and narrow the board for a way-marker.

defaults.rationale: 2.62 m clears a 1.7 m figure walking under the board by a comfortable margin, which is the proportion that makes a hanging sign read as a street sign.
